messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: New version is out
parts:
INLA_22.03.24 is there now with quite a few internal changes (especially
for data-rich models and 'experimental' mode), so it is slightly more
'testing' than usual. Please be aware.

There was a regression bug in INLA_22.02.16 using
control.inla=list(strategy="laplace") that is now fixed in
INLA_22.03.24. Sorry about that one. The version in 'stable',
INLA_22.03.16, is also affected by this issue, but will be updated asap
we know there are no issues with this version.

The internal calculations have changed slightly for output compuations
and merging of marginal densities, so the results will be tiny different
compared to earlier versions. The mode of the density is now most often
reported as NA unless its know, as its to expensive to compute if one
does not need it.

If there is anything, please email he...@r-inla.org

Best
H
--
Håvard Rue
hr...@r-inla.org

Hi Håvard,

Great to know that the INLA_22.03.24 is out now. I have installed a testing version in my Windows 10 and ran spatiotemporal models with covariates, spatial, temporal and spatiotemporal random effect models. The input for a type IV interaction model needs output 'mode' from a previously run model. As per the new INLA, all output for mode is 'NA'. How can I get the output for 'mode' for running the subsequent model? or can I use the mean instead. Kindly clarify.

Regards
S. Subramanian
